Slide 1 · 0:00April sixteenth, twenty twenty-four. Two hundred fifty-four millimetres of rain, the heaviest in seventy-five years of UAE records. Everyone remembers the water. Banks should remember how long it stayed.
Slide 2 · 0:18Banks model how deep the water gets. Dubai's lesson was how long it stayed. Three days after the rain stopped, ninety-five percent of the flooded area was still under water. On day ten, thirty-seven percent. A shop that can't open can't repay. Yet the Central Bank's stress test leaves lost revenue out of scope.
Slide 3 · 0:44So here is what's new. Depth at the collateral drives the loss if a loan defaults. The days water stayed around the business drive the chance that it defaults, and that is the part the stress test leaves out. One storm, two losses, priced together, loan by loan.
Slide 4 · 1:10This is CLIMAX. A Sentinel-2 pass comes in and we find the new water. Now watch the days go by: every building gets a count of how long the water stayed. Join that to the loan book. Duration lifts probability of default, depth lifts loss given default, and loans hit on both light up. An analyst asks in Arabic, and the agent answers with tool calls you can audit. One click gives the risk committee a memo with every scene ID, assumption and limitation. These loans are synthetic; the pilot swaps in a real book.
Slide 5 · 1:56One engine, four winners. Banks get a review queue after the first clear satellite pass, not after the first missed payment. Insurers get accumulation and claims triage. The Central Bank gets a district-level view. Residents get steadier housing finance. And the data is free and open.
Slide 6 · 2:20Ninety days. Weeks one and two: geocode one bank's SME book on its own systems. Three and four: replay April on real loans. Five to eight: calibrate on real arrears and insurer claims. Nine and ten: into the risk committee. Eleven and twelve: a go or no-go for three banks.
Slide 7 · 2:44Banks model how deep. CLIMAX measures how long. Our ask: one bank, one CBUAE sandbox, ninety days. Thank you.
